relations.myth: The tree, bull, and three cranes
relations.note: Esus cuts a tree beside or within a scene featuring the bull.
relations.source: Pillar of the Boatmen and Trier relief

relations.myth: Lucan's catalogue of blood-appeased Gallic gods
relations.note: Lucan names Teutates immediately before Esus without describing an interaction.

relations.myth: Gauls appease both gods with human blood
relations.note: Lactantius jointly names Esus and Teutates as recipients of human blood.

relations.myth: Lucan's catalogue of blood-appeased Gallic gods
relations.note: Lucan names Taranis immediately after Esus without describing an interaction.
One scholiastic interpretive scheme equates Esus with Mars.
An alternative scholiastic interpretive scheme equates Esus with Mercury.
Mercury and the probable Esus woodcutter appear as distinct figures on one monument.

relations.myth: Pillar of the Boatmen divine assemblage
relations.note: Esus and Jupiter appear on different faces of the same monument.

relations.myth: Pillar of the Boatmen divine assemblage
relations.note: Esus and Vulcan share the monument, but no episode connects them.

relations.myth: Pillar of the Boatmen divine assemblage
relations.note: Both gods are named on the same monument without interaction.

relations.myth: Pillar of the Boatmen divine assemblage
relations.note: Both beings occur on the same monument without interaction.

relations.myth: Pillar of the Boatmen divine assemblage
relations.note: The divine twins and Esus share the monument without interaction.
A probable Rosmerta image shares the monument with the probable Esus scene.
